newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia honours reporter killed in 1991 siege.
newsitem.headline: Croatia honours reporter killed in 1991 siege.

text.p: A Croatian radio journalist apparently executed by Serbian forces for his dramatic reports from besieged Vukovar in 1991 was ceremonially buried on Friday in a memorial service attended by thousands.

The remains of Sinisa Glavasevic were recently identified among 200 bodies of Croat execution victims unearthed from a mass grave near Vukovar in Eastern Slavonia, a Serb enclave of Croatia due to revert to central government rule this summer.

War-crimes investigators say the 200 were primarily Vukovar hospital patients shot after the city fell to Serb forces in November 1991, near the end of Croatia's war for independence from Serbian-led federal Yugoslavia.

The war ended with Serb rebels holding Vukovar and its Slavonian hinterland but the region will now be reintegrated under U.N. supervision with the rest of Croatia after Croatian army victories over Serb separatists elsewhere in the country.
Glavasevic's persistent radio reports from Vukovar bomb shelters during the 100-day siege made him a Croatian national hero before he disappeared without a trace as the city fell.
His fate was unknown until his remains were identified among the Ovcara mass grave victims.
Several thousand people attended the funeral at Zagreb's crematorium, including scores of Croatian government officials, dignitaries and journalists as well as his family and friends.
"Your memory will warm our hearts for a long time to come," said Alemka Mirkovic Nadj, Glavasevic's former colleague at Vukovar regional radio.

"We are saying farewell to Sinisa Glavasevic who brought us encouragement during the most difficult times and whose reports gave us hope during the 100 days," said a Croat Catholic parish priest from Vukovar, Branimir Kosec.
